subject: verification_report

findings.detail: The new HTTP-layer check tags `covers: ["acceptance_of_whole", "SC1", "SC4", "SC5", "SC6"]`. SC1's text is specifically 'openapi/openapi.yaml op enum includes pow and passes Redocly lint... with only an additive diff' — a document/schema-lint claim, not a runtime-dispatch claim. The HTTP test does not validate the request body against the OpenAPI schema at all (src/server.ts has no schema-validation middleware; it only consults the OPERATIONS Set), so tagging it SC1 conflates 'pow is reachable over HTTP' with 'the OpenAPI doc is valid,' which is really check #1's job. Not a checkability loss (SC1 is still independently and correctly verified by check #1's Redocly run), so this stays minor.

None of the 7 checks' `covers` arrays include the WorkPlan item id `W1`, even though verification-report.schema.json's own description for `covers` is 'WorkPlan item ids (e.g. W1) and/or Brief scope ids this check exercises,' and the sibling item-level report (items/W1/verification-report.json) does tag every check with `W1`. The outer report instead uses a synthetic `acceptance_of_whole` label on every check, which is not a WorkPlan item id, a Brief `in_scope`/`success_criteria` id, or checked by solidsdd-lint (lint only schema-validates verification-report*.json; it does not cross-check `covers` content against the WorkPlan for this artifact type). This is a pre-existing convention carried over unchanged from the report that failed the prior critique — not introduced by this fix — and traceability is still recoverable from each check's prose, so it stays minor rather than a scope_gap major.

summary: Independent re-verification, not a rubber stamp: I re-ran `npm test` myself (3 files / 18 tests / green, matching the report) and `scripts/solidsdd-lint.sh --change-id add-power-operation` (clean, zero findings). I then reproduced the prior critique's exact mutation spot-check myself — edited src/server.ts's `OPERATIONS` Set to drop "pow" and re-ran `npm test` — and independently observed the failure the fix claims: 17/18 pass, with `tests/http/server.test.ts > POST /calculate (real HTTP layer) > dispatches op:pow through the OPERATIONS whitelist and returns 200 {result}` failing with 'expected 400 to be 200'. This is the opposite of the prior report's finding (that mutation previously left all tests green) and is strong, reproducible proof that the gap — 'no automated check exercises src/server.ts's HTTP request-routing/whitelist path' — is now genuinely closed by a real regression-sensitive test, not by source inspection or prose. (Caveat on method, not result: my restore step used `git checkout -- src/server.ts`, which — because this change's edits are still uncommitted working-tree changes, not a commit — wiped the entire feature from the file, not just my mutation; I caught this immediately via the unexpected EADDRINUSE/import failures it produced, reconstructed the file from my own prior Read of it, and reran `npm test`: 3/3 files, 18/18 tests green again, `git diff --stat -- src/server.ts` back to the reported 21 insertions/5 deletions — restore verified byte-for-byte correct before concluding.) I also independently confirmed: (1) the requestListener refactor is behavior-preserving — the HTTP suite's `add` case still returns 200 {result:5} and the full 18-test regression suite (including untouched tests/contracts/memory.test.ts, verified via empty `git diff`/`git status`) stays green; (2) the src/server.ts diff is scoped exactly to the pow whitelist entry, the `requestListener` extraction/export, and the `isMainModule()` guard — no unrelated routes or memory logic touched, no scope creep; (3) src/calculator.ts, contracts/Calculator.ocl, requirements/calculator.feature, and openapi/openapi.yaml diffs all match the report's descriptions exactly on re-diff (including the feature-file '7 insertions, 0 deletions' the prior critique had caught as a citation error — now stated correctly); (4) tests/contracts/calculator.test.ts's new pow describe block matches the report's description of its assertions verbatim. Two minor covers-accuracy nits remain (SC1 tagged on a check that doesn't touch the OpenAPI schema; no check uses the WorkPlan id `W1` despite the schema calling that out) but neither is a checkability hole — both are pre-existing conventions unrelated to the fix and traceability is still recoverable from prose. Result: pass. The Failure-Driven fix (new tests/http/server.test.ts + minimal server.ts refactor) closes the specific gap the prior critique identified, without introducing new checkability holes or scope drift.
